title: Instantaneous Haphazard Slash
text: Ren is muttering to himself as if he has some idea what’s going on.
“Who are you talking about?”
“That’s enough already. My childhood friend has found someone else to like! That’s fine!”
Ren is trying to wrap up the conversation. He sounds pretty resigned.
“As for the rest…”
“Are you really going to keep this up?!”
“I’m going to reenact right here the training Gaelion gave me at my request when I faced the Sword Hero of the First World.”
The Rival suddenly shifts into his young dragon form, makes several pieces of lumber lying nearby float in the air—each the size of a sword—and, floating himself, takes a fighting stance facing Ren.
“Hmm!”
The moment he saw that movement, Ren reflexively drew his sword and took a stance.
“Here I go—”
With that, the Rival manipulated countless pieces of lumber in midair, launching them at Ren. Ren, meanwhile, charged forward, fending off the countless flying pieces of lumber with his sword.
“Haaaaaaah!”
“Oops… that was close.”
The Rival swiftly dodged Ren’s horizontal slash by stepping back, then lunged forward, sweeping a square timber horizontally toward Ren’s back as they passed each other.
“Haa!”
Ren crouched to avoid the attack from behind and charged straight at the Rival.
“Wooooooah!”
And just like that, they both became completely engrossed in the battle. Ren is fighting with an incredibly lively expression. He looks absolutely thrilled.
“Let’s pick up the pace!”

The speed of the wooden beams the rival was floating increased, and Ren got more and more fired up in response, but he couldn’t keep up. Just as a beam flying in from a blind spot clattered into him, all the surrounding beams fell to the ground.
“Ugh…”
With a frustrated groan, Ren slumped his shoulders in defeat—but then suddenly snapped back to his senses.
“It’s useless trying to awaken me!”
He readjusted his glasses. That’s completely unconvincing.
“Really… It seems Ren from the first world was quite ‘awakened,’ wasn’t he?”
“Hmm… It didn’t feel like ‘awakening’ so much as just moving toward his goal. The Sword Hero isn’t great at using floating weapons, but he really enjoys fighting enemies.”
“Huh, I see.”
Ren looks away from us.
“If anything, this is the one that really ‘awakens’ you.”
Saying that, my rival picks up a vegetable lying near my Father, who’s in the middle of cooking.
“Naofumi, let your stats handle this—slice and separate the vegetable in midair. Hurry up and cook it so we can get this done.”
With that, my rival tosses the vegetable toward Father with a “plop.”
“Huh!? Wait a sec!?”

My father, who was holding a kitchen knife, instinctively did as he was told and sliced the vegetable in midair with his knife. First, he aligned the blade vertically with the skin and pushed down with a single stroke—the skin peeled off in a straight line—then followed up with a series of swift, flowing slashes. The haphazardly chopped vegetables were dumped into the pot with a clatter. This is the cooking method my wild father uses when he’s in a hurry. Even my father can do this, you know.
Ren and Itsuki fell silent, and even the Assistant just stood there staring blankly.
“Gaelion-chan, could you please not just suddenly throw this at me?”
“Naaah~”
“I told you this cutting method makes it really sloppy… and the cut surfaces end up a mess, too. I guess I’ll just use it for sauce or something…”
With a look that says “Seriously…” my Father sighs. I get it. It’s got to do with the fibers in the ingredients, right?
“I wonder why Naofumi-san wasn’t summoned as a Sword Hero?”
“What are you talking about all of a sudden?”
“Is that cutting technique something you copied from a manga or something?”
“Huh? Yeah. I just thought it looked cool, so I imitated it and picked it up. It’s not that hard in this world.”
“No… it doesn’t look difficult at all—it looks like a master-class technique to me.”

“Really? In my circle, it’s a bit of a running joke—people are surprised at first when I show it off, but after I do it a few times, they just roll with it… Also, cutting like this breaks down the fibers, which ruins the flavor and limits the dishes you can use it in.”
Isn’t that just because the people around you have such refined palates?
“I’ll ask you straight up: can you toss the ingredients into a pot or bowl right after you cut them?”
“You mean this?”
With that, my father began chopping the vegetables and simultaneously flinging them into the pot. As expected of my Father.
“Naofumi, don’t let the Sword Hero and Black Thunder watch this.”
“Huh?”
Ren and Black Thunder are standing side by side, looking at my Father with sparkling eyes.
“Ren, he’s got that look that says, ‘My heart is yearning to awaken!’”
“Ugh… I can’t let myself awaken!”
With a *snap*, Ren readjusted his thick-rimmed glasses.
“…Tell me how to do it later.”
“Yeah, yeah…”
He hasn’t graduated at all. It’s only a matter of time before he awakens.
“If we keep talking like this, Gaelion’s going to tease us… Let’s save this conversation for another day. I’m tired.”
“So this is what they mean by ‘stirring up trouble,’ huh?”
“Itsuki, someday I’m going to make Gaelion spill the beans on one of your embarrassing stories.”
“If there’s something even more impressive than ‘Perfect Hide Justice,’ I’d love to hear about it.”
His Rival asks Itsuki this right here, looking him straight in the face.
“Isn’t ‘Perfect Justice: Filolial Mask V3’ impressive?”
“That’s just a further development, and since it’s a similar gimmick designed to counter Fleon, it’s nothing to be embarrassed about.”
“True, it might not pack quite as much of a punch compared to Perfect Hide Justice.”
“Compared to ‘Filolial Cross!’, it’s definitely not as impressive.”
“Is he still around?”
“He’s the Wise King of Wisdom.”
“Even Aultcray? Seriously… it’s endless. That king, though…”
“A Trash who realized the truth transforms into a masked hero who unites different races.”
“That’s definitely not going to end well, is it? And it’s not even my topic anyway.”
We’re getting off track here. Is it about Itsuki? Did something happen on par with Ren’s awakening or something? All we have is that he’s good friends with Fleon-chan.
“Hmm…”
Ren, who had looked frustrated, suddenly had a look of inspiration and gave Itsuki a smirk.
“What is it?”
“Itsuki… you’re pretty low-key when it comes to anything other than Fleon.”
“Guh! It’s better than being made fun of endlessly!”
“Listen up. Indifference is worse than being disliked.”
“Ugh… There’s no benefit in thinking you’ve won over something like this.”
“You two, stop fighting, okay?”

Ren was laughing as if he’d won. Well, the first Itsuki set out on a journey to set the world right with Riska, but other than that, there aren’t really any particularly noteworthy stories about him. Ren, on the other hand, never ran out of material. I guess, in the end, it’s all thanks to Riska that Itsuki turned out the way he did.
“Fleon, you’ve got to instill more justice in Itsuki. Take off those headphones and sing!”
Ren is cheering on Fleon-chan as if seizing the perfect moment.
“You mustn’t do things he genuinely hates. This means my sense of justice hasn’t reached Itsuki-san yet! So I’m going to keep honing my sense of justice!”
And with that, Fleon-chan’s eyes blazed with fighting spirit. Surely the day will come when Fleon-chan’s singing overpowers Itsuki’s sneaky headphones, and he’ll finally awaken to justice.
“It’d be nice if we could convince Itsuki with words.”
“I’ve graduated from justice, too.”
With a swish, Itsuki puts on the thick-lensed glasses Ren is wearing, adopting a full-on otaku look.
“Did you know? Once you graduate from middle school and justice, you catch a disease called ‘high school sophomore’—where you mock those things and come to love compromise and sound reasoning.”
“It really does come down to effort over talent. From now on, it’s an era of living down-to-earth.”
“Aren’t you kind of shooting yourselves in the foot here? Are you two really okay with that?”
“Well then… enough with the break and the small talk—let’s go build our safe haven.”
“Yeah… let’s go!”
“Let’s do it!”
Just what kind of “country bumpkin” vibe are they going for here? It seems they’re going all out in a style that Fleon-chan and Black Thunder definitely wouldn’t approve of.
“Naofumi, let me know when dinner’s ready—we’re about to eat!”
“Where on earth did these two get their sense of style?”
“It’s actually kind of funny in its own way.”
It was striking that our Rival was laughing.
“Oh my—”
“I wonder what they’re up to…”
The Big Sister and the Panda let out exasperated sighs as they watched us. Then, Itsuki came back and whispered,
“Wearing glasses without a prescription to pretend to be an ordinary person is pretty much ‘chuunibyou,’ isn’t it?”
Itsuki in this world is just the same as ever.

Kou, who seemed to be having fun playing with Yuki-chan, Fleon-chan, and the others, suddenly found himself quietly gazing up at the sky in his Filolial form. He seems fine, more or less, but compared to the Kou from previous loops, he seems a bit less energetic.
“Are you worried about Kou, the Spear Hero?”
“I’d be worried about any Filolial-sama, no matter who it is! What’s going on? If you do anything to Kou, I won’t forgive you!”
“Yeah, yeah… Well, I pretty much know the reason, so I’ll figure something out when the time is right.”
And with that, my Rival made an ominous remark. What on earth does she plan to do to Kou!? No… I feel like I have a vague idea myself. It’s a way to cheer up a downcast Kou.

As for the rest… Well, the moles heard about our plans to rebuild the village and rushed over to help. I’ve also heard that Éclair and my Finacée have agreed to help rebuild the neighboring town as well. Since the Hero is leading the reconstruction efforts, not only is Melromarc contributing, but aid supplies are occasionally arriving from other nations as well.

This happened a little while after we’d started the village reconstruction work. Since it’s not good to burn out from working too hard on the reconstruction, our Rival suggested we all take a break and go out, so we decided to head to Zeltoble.

By the way, Yuki-chan often goes out to participate in Filolial races. In this world, we entrust Yuki-chan and the others to Filolial producers so they can enter them in the races. I’ve heard that ever since the turmoil ended and peace was restored, the atmosphere has become livelier, and races are being held more and more frequently.

Naturally, we went to watch the Filolial races featuring Yuki-chan and the others—the Filolial-samas we’ve raised. We were told that Yuki-chan’s Big Sister—who used to be a famous fighter in Zeltoble—and Panda would be there as escorts, so they figured that even if something went wrong, they’d be able to handle it to some extent. Plus, since the Filolial-sama are here too, the village slaves are safe as well.
“Zeltoble really has everything when it comes to entertainment, doesn’t it?”
“Yeah—I wonder if there’s anything money can’t solve.”
“We talked before about how places with lots of mini-games tend to be like that.”
With that sort of banter, we all strolled around Zeltoble together.
“It feels nostalgic even though not that much time has passed, doesn’t it?”
“We were living such intense, packed days back then.”
Right now, we’ve just entered the Zeltoble Colosseum to watch a match.
“If I weren’t in this condition, I’d jump right in here for a round to blow off some steam, just for fun.”
“Um…”
As my Father stammers, looking flustered, Panda waves her hand as if to say, “Don’t worry about it.”
“Sasa-chan’s a bit of a troublemaker, isn’t she? You’re not short on money, are you? Do you still need more?”
“It’s my hobby. I won’t let you complain.”
“Panda donates the money she earns, you know.”
Come to think of it, Panda does provide financial support to the Tiger siblings. She’s just not the type to admit it.
“Is that so?”
“It is.”
The Rival traveling with us nods. Then my father looked at Panda with admiration.
“Lars-chan, that’s amazing!”
“You—where did you… ugh…”
Panda furrowed her brow, looked at me, and fell silent. “How do you know?” you might ask.
“Of course, it’s knowledge I gained from the loop. It was a donation to the Tiger siblings, whom Ren and Itsuki are already taking care of.”
“What!?”

Fohl, who had been standing off to the side with the village slaves, spoke up. He’s as unassuming as ever, but he’s definitely here. It seems Tiger Girl is staying behind to mind the house this time. Riska is also staying behind with her. After all, she’s in the middle of proposing the elegant life of royalty to her Finacée.
“Is that so!?”
“Don’t worry about it. I was just throwing money away out of self-satisfaction back when I was rolling in it!”
“But…”
The Tiger Guy looks apologetic toward the Panda.
“If you think of it as a thank-you, you’ve got it all wrong. I only did it because your dad saved me, and you don’t need it anymore, right?”
After all, the Tiger Girl has already been treated by Ren and Itsuki. The expense is practically nothing.
“If you want to repay me, then become a great person. That’s what I want from you.”
“…I understand. I promise.”
“Lars-chan, you’re so cool!”
“Sasa-chan, you’re killing it! That’s so awesome!”
“Hey, you two! Don’t make fun of him!”
That’s the kind of exchange they’re having. I’m so happy to see the fathers-in-law getting along so well.
